title: CLCON/482/2021 of M/S R P G INFRATECH REGISTERED OFFICE Vs DARBAN SINGH NAYAL

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Contempt Petition No. 482 of 2021
M/s RPG Infratech. ................Petitioner.

Through: Shri Piyush Garg, learned counsel
for the petitioner.
-Versus-Mr. Darban Singh Nayal
and another. .........Respondents.
Through: Ms. Anusuya Salwan, Sr. Advocate
assisted by Shri Hari Mohan Bhatia, learned
counsel for respondents.
Date of hearing and Judgment : 04.11.2022
Shri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
1. In this petition, petitioner has approached this Court to
summon and punish the respondent nos. 1 and 2 for deliberately
disobeying the order passed by this Court. Petitioner is a
registered firm. It complains that there has been a willful
violation of the order dated 16.09.2019 passed by this Court in
Criminal Misc. Application No. 1477 of 2018.
2. Initially, the Directors of M/s MBL Infrastructure Ltd., a
registered company, (hereinafter referred to as "Company" for
brevity) filed an application, under Section 482 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "CrPC" for
brevity), bearing No. 1600 of 2017 for quashing of the summoning
order passed by learned Magistrate under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as "NI
Act" for brevity). The said application was dismissed by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 04.07.2018.
Against the order dated 04.07.2018, the Company preferred
Special Leave to Appeal No. 7083 of 2018 before the Hon'ble

2
Supreme Court. The Supreme Court vide order dated 04.09.2018
dismissed the same. Thereafter, the Company along with
respondent no. 2, herein, preferred a petition under Section 482 of
the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 before this Court, which
was disposed of on 16.09.2019. For proper appreciation of the
issue involved in this case, the entire order passed by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court is quoted as under:
"Shri A.S. Rawat, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr.
Sarawat Mahapatra and Mr. Lalit Sharma, Advocate for
the applicant. Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the
respondent.
The present application has been filed by the
applicant under Section C-482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the
impugned summoning order dated 25.07.2017 in Criminal
Case No. 109 of 2017 (RPG Infratech Versus MBL
Infrastructures Ltd. and other), pending before the Court of
Judicial Magistrate, Ranikhet District Almora.
The respondent - M/s RPG Infratech filed an
application under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments
Act, against the applicant and others regarding the cheque
amount of Rs 1,35,84,099/- dated 13.03.2017.
During the course of hearing the learned Sr. counsel
appearing on behalf of the applicant, argued that the cheque
dated 13.03.2017, amounting to Rs. 1,35,84,099/- which
was issued by the applicant in favour of respondent-RPG
Infratech MBL Infrastructures Ltd. and other companies,
the applicant- company is ready to pay the said amount to
the respondent.
It is also argued by learned Sr. counsel for the
applicant that the proceeding before the National Company
Law Tribunal (NCLT) is started on 30.03.2017 and
Interim Resolution Professional was appointed on the same

3
day and the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
passed the final order dated 18.04.2018 in which the
respondent had already submitted their claims including
the present cheque dated 13.03.2017, amounting Rs.
1,35,84,099/-.
It is also argued that, as per the National Company
Law Tribunal (NCLT) order dated 13.03.2017, the
company is bound to pay the said amount issued by the
company in favour of the respondent. The company is ready
to pay the said amount within a period of 20 months from
today.
The proceedings will start after a period of 20
months, since the applicant's company will pay the
aforesaid cheque amount within a period of 20 (twenty)
months.
In these circumstances, the present C 482 application
is disposed of finally with the direction that the applicant
will pay the above amount to the respondent within a
period of 20 months from today. In case non-payment of the
said amount, the lower court has a right to proceed against
the present applicants after completion of 20 months, as per
the law.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of."
3. However, the company could not satisfy the undertaking
given and therefore, it filed an application for extension of time,
which came before the Coordinate Bench of this Court and on
19.04.2021, the same was also dismissed. Thereafter, present
contempt petition has been filed.
4. Before coming to the issue, in question, it is appropriate to
take note of certain dates and events.

4
On 18.09.2014, an agreement was executed between the
Company and Public Works Department, Dehradun.
On 20.02.2015, work order was executed between the
Company and M/s RPG Infratech for part work of improvement
and strengthening of roads.
On 18.07.2016, contract between the company and PWD
was terminated.
On 30.03.2017, Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of
the Company was initiated under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy
Code, 2016 (hereinafter referred to as "IBC" for brevity).
Moratorium was declared and powers of Board of Directors were
suspended and the management of the Company was vested
with Insolvency Resolution Professional appointed by NCLT,
Kolkata.
On 13.04.2017, M/s RPG Infratech filed a claim before the
Insolvency Resolution Professional.
On 08.05.2017, a cheque bearing no. 639991 dated 13.03.2017
was dishonoured by the Bank.
On 25.07.2017, a Complaint Case bearing no. 109 of 2017
was filed before Judicial Magistrate, Ranikhet under Section 138
of the N.I. Act. The Court took the cognizance of the offence and
issued summoning order dated 25.07.2017.
On 16.08.2019, all the appeals filed by different parties
against the resolution plan was dismissed by the National
Company Law Appellate Tribunal.
On 25.11.2019, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal
No. 8411 of 2019 filed by Bank of Baroda stayed order dated
16.08.2019 passed by NCLAT.

5
The order, which violation is alleged in the case, was
passed on 16.09.2019 by the Coordinate Bench of this Court. Time
so granted expired in the month of April, 2021. Time extension
application filed by the Company was dismissed by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court on 19.04.2021.
On 21.11.2021, present Civil Contempt Petition No. 482 of
2021 was filed by M/s RPG Infratech.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that as on
the date, when the order was passed by the Coordinate Bench,
violation of which is asserted in this case, entire proceedings of
IBC were completed, hence, the Directors of the Company shall
be liable under their personal capacity for contempt. He would
rely upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of
P. Mohanraj and others Vs. Shah Brothers Ispat Pvt. Ltd. (2021)
6 SCC 258 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court considered the
scope and applicability of Section 14 read with Section 7 to 9 of
the IBC with regard to proceedings under Section 138 & 141 of
the NI Act against the corporate debtor. The Hon'ble Supreme
Court has held that since the corporate debtor would be covered
by the moratorium provision contained in Section 14 IBC, by
which continuation of Sections 138/141 proceedings against the
corporate debtor and initiation of Sections 138/141 proceedings
against the said debtor during the corporate insolvency
resolution process are interdicted, what is stated in paras 51 and
59 in Aneeta Hada Vs. Godfather Travels & Tours (P) Ltd.,
(2012) 5 SCC 661 would then become applicable. The legal
impediment contained in Section 14 IBC would make it
impossible for such proceeding to continue or be instituted
against the corporate debtor. Thus, for the period of moratorium,
since no Sections 138/141 proceeding can continue or be initiated

6
against the corporate debtor because of a statutory bar, such
proceedings can be initiated or continued against the persons
mentioned in Sections 141(1) and (2) of the Negotiable
Instruments Act. This being the case, it is clear that the
moratorium provision contained in Section 14 IBC would apply
only to the corporate debtor, the natural persons mentioned in
Section 141 continuing to be statutorily liable under Chapter XVII
of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Thus, it was held that
proceedings under Section 138/141 of the NI Act shall continue
against the Company as well as appellants, who are Directors of
the Company
6. For proper appreciation of the case, Section 14 of the IBC
reads as under:
"14. Moratorium.-(1) Subject to provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3), on the insolvency commencement
date, the adjudicating authority shall by order declare
moratorium for prohibiting all of the following,
namely-
(a) the institution of suits or continuation of
pending suits or proceedings against the corporate
debtor including execution of any judgment, decree
or order in any court of law, tribunal, arbitration
panel or other authority;
(b) transferring, encumbering, alienating or
disposing of by the corporate debtor any of its assets
or any legal right or beneficial interest therein;
(c) any action to foreclose, recover or enforce any
security interest created by the corporate debtor in
respect of its property including any action under
the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial

7
Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act,
2002 (54 of 2002);
(d) the recovery of any property by an owner or
lessor where such property is occupied by or in the
possession of the corporate debtor.
Explanation.-For the purposes of this sub-section, it is hereby clarified that notwithstanding
anything contained in any other law for the time
being in force, a licence, permit, registration, quota,
concession, clearances or a similar grant or right
given by the Central Government, State
Government, local authority, sectoral regulator or
any other authority constituted under any other law
for the time being in force, shall not be suspended or
terminated on the grounds of insolvency, subject to
the condition that there is no default in payment of
current dues arising for the use or continuation of
the licence, permit, registration, quota, concession,
clearances or a similar grant or right during the
moratorium period.
(2) The supply of essential goods or services to the
corporate debtor as may be specified shall not be
terminated or suspended or interrupted during
moratorium period.
(2-A) Where the interim resolution professional or
resolution professional, as the case may be, considers the
supply of goods or services critical to protect and
preserve the value of the corporate debtor and manage
the operations of such corporate debtor as a going
concern, then the supply of such goods or services shall
not be terminated, suspended or interrupted during the
period of moratorium, except where such corporate

8
debtor has not paid dues arising from such supply
during the moratorium period or in such circumstances
as may be specified.
(3) The provisions of sub-section (1) shall not apply to-
(a) such transactions, agreements or other
arrangements as may be notified by the
Central Government in consultation with any
financial sector regulator or any other
authority;
(b) a surety in a contract of guarantee to a
corporate debtor.
(4) The order of moratorium shall have effect from the
date of such order till the completion of the corporate
insolvency resolution process:
Provided that where at any time during the
corporate insolvency resolution process period, if the
adjudicating authority approves the resolution plan
under sub-section (1) of Section 31 or passes an order
for liquidation of corporate debtor under Section 33, the
moratorium shall cease to have effect from the date of
such approval or liquidation order, as the case may be."
7. A plain reading of aforesaid provision reveals that subject
to the exceptions contained in sub-sections (2) and (3), on the date
of commencement of insolvency, the adjudicating authority shall
mandatorily, by order, declare a moratorium to prohibit what
follows in clauses (a) to (d). Importantly, under sub-section (4),
this order of moratorium does not continue indefinitely, but has
effect only from the date of the order declaring moratorium till
the completion of the corporate insolvency resolution process
which is time-bound, either culminating in the order of the

9
adjudicating authority approving a resolution plan or in
liquidation.
8. In this case, it is not disputed by the parties that on
30.03.2017, corporate insolvency resolution process of the
company was initiated by National Company Law Tribunal,
Kolkata. A copy of the order dated 30.03.2017 passed by National
Company Law Tribunal, Kolkata is Annexure No. R 17 to the
contempt petition. In the insolvency proceedings, the National
Company Law Tribunal appointed Mr. Atanu Mukherjee,
Advocate, Supreme Court of India, as an Interim Resolution
Professional. In the last paragraph of the said order, appearing at
page no. 234 of the paper book, the Tribunal admitted the petition
for initiating the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process and
declared a moratorium and public announcement, as stated in
Section 13 of the IBC, 2016. Necessary public announcement, as
per Section 15 of the IBC 2016 has been made by the applicant
company. It is further provided that Mr. Atanu Mukherjee was
appointed as Interim Resolution Professional, who would initiate
the process, as per Rules. A public announcement was made,
copy whereof is Annexure R 18 to the response affidavit.
9. It is also not disputed that M/s RPG Infratech filed a claim
before Insolvency Resolution Professional on 13.04.2017 and
thereafter, presented a cheque which was dishonoured on
08.05.2017. Thus, it is clear that on the date i.e. on 16.09.2019,
when the undertaking was given by the company that it would
pay the amount within 20 months, insolvency process was
underway and had come its logical conclusion, thereafter. On a
month prior to that, all the appeals were dismissed by the
National Company Law Appellate Tribunal. Still the forum of
approaching the Hon'ble Supreme Court was not exhausted.

10
10. In that view of the matter, it is clear that contemnors /
respondents on account of reasons that are reasonable, genuine
and beyond their control, could not perform their part of the
undertaking.
11. In this case, the Court relies upon the reported judgment of
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Suman Chadha and
another Vs. Central Bank of India, (2021) SCC Online 564,
wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that in appropriate
cases where a party had acted bonafide while giving an
undertaking, but could not honour the undertaking on account of
reasons that are reasonable and genuine, the Court could
certainly withhold its stick from being wielded.
12. But in this case there are findings of fact to the effect that
the petitioners did act in a bona fide manner in the sense that
they had given an undertaking to pay money but as per the final
order of the NCLT dated 18.04.2018, the resolution plan was
approved. The same was appealed before the Appellate Tribunal
and the Hon'ble Supreme Court, so this Court is of the
considered view that the conduct of the contemnors /
respondents passes the test of reasonableness and bona fide and
therefore, the case to punish the respondents is not made out and
accordingly, the Contempt proceeding is dropped.
 (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.) (Grant urgent certified copy of this judgment, as per Rules)
SKS
